stories.headline: Ultra Lounge East Owner to Surrender Liquor and Cabaret Licenses Following Mass Shooting
stories.summary:
The owner of a Denver nightclub that was the site of a mass shooting last month has agreed to surrender his liquor and cabaret licenses under a settlement with the city. The shooting at Ultra Lounge East, located at 9755 E. Hampden Ave., killed Elijah Bernard, 25, and injured eight others in the early morning hours of July 20.

The settlement order, issued Wednesday by Denver's Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, identifies Dol Bhattarai as the license holder. Bhattarai admitted to several violations including disorderly behavior, unauthorized transfer of ownership, and failure to report a change of trade name. Investigators found that Bhattarai had sold or subleased the property to Dionte Wilkins without notifying city or state authorities.

Under the terms of the agreement, the surrender of the licenses will be treated as a revocation, barring the listed owner from reapplying for a liquor license for at least one year. Previous violations cited in the suspension order included an unlicensed security guard injuring a patron and a man killed during a beating in the parking lot.

Denver Police investigators said evidence showed at least two people fired shots during the July 20 incident, with 66 shell casings — both .45 caliber and 9mm — found inside the premises and on the patio. As of Wednesday, no arrests have been made in the shooting.

stories.headline: Aurora Police Seek White Subaru Outback in Fatal Hit-and-Run That Killed Bicyclist
stories.summary:
The Aurora Police Department is asking for the public's help in identifying a 2015-2019 white Subaru Outback connected to a fatal hit-and-run crash that killed a bicyclist on July 26. The crash occurred just after midnight on S. Powhaton Road, approximately a quarter mile north of E. Jewell Avenue, when the driver struck a southbound bicyclist and fled the scene.

The victim was not discovered until the following morning. Traffic cameras captured the suspect vehicle traveling southbound on Gun Club Road at E. Quincy Avenue at approximately 12:12 a.m., roughly 12 minutes after the crash.

Police say the Subaru Outback will likely have damage to the front passenger-side headlight and hood, a missing passenger-side fog light, and possibly a cracked driver-side headlight. The vehicle's description and damage pattern are key identifying features investigators are relying on.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Metro Denver CrimeStoppers at 720-913-STOP (7867) and reference case number 26-155696. Callers may remain anonymous and could be eligible for a reward of up to $2,000.

stories.headline: Pedestrian Struck by Bus on East Colfax Avenue in Denver
stories.summary:
A pedestrian was injured Tuesday evening after being hit by a bus on East Colfax Avenue in Denver, temporarily shutting down a stretch of the busy corridor. Denver Police first reported the crash near East Colfax Avenue and Verbena Street at approximately 6:25 p.m.

Colfax Avenue was closed in both directions between Verbena and Valentina streets to allow for crash cleanup and investigation. The closure affected the East Colfax neighborhood in eastern Denver.

Additional details about the pedestrian's condition and the circumstances of the crash had not been released as of Wednesday morning. The Denver Post described the story as developing and said it may be updated as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Indian Creek Fire Forces Mandatory Evacuations in Jackson County
stories.summary:
A new wildfire ignited in Jackson County in northern Colorado on Tuesday, prompting mandatory evacuations for residents along Jackson County Road 53, also known as Forest Service Road 103. The fire, dubbed the Indian Creek Fire, is burning in a forested area approximately 20 miles east of Steamboat Springs near the Wyoming border in one of Colorado's least populated counties.

As of the morning of August 5, the fire was estimated at 15 acres and moving eastward, with ground crews and aerial assets — including a firefighting plane and helicopter — working to contain it. Voluntary pre-evacuation notices were also issued for portions of Highway 14 from 1B to Jackson County Road 11A.

Jackson County issued a red flag warning for Wednesday, with wind gusts expected to reach 35 to 40 mph between noon and 7 p.m. and relative humidity levels forecast to drop to between 7% and 14%, creating dangerous fire weather conditions.

No injuries or structure losses had been reported as of Wednesday morning. Authorities recommended residents download the Watch Duty app and sign up for local alerts by texting JALERTS to 888777.

stories.headline: CPW Lethally Removes Uncollared Wolf in Grand County Following Multiple Livestock Depredations
stories.summary:
Colorado Parks and Wildlife announced Wednesday that it lethally removed an uncollared yearling wolf from Grand County after the animal was linked to multiple confirmed livestock depredation incidents. The wolf was killed on August 4 and was identified as a member of the One Ear pack.

The removal followed four confirmed depredation events attributed to the wolf. CPW protocol allows for lethal removal of wolves that repeatedly prey on livestock after other measures have been considered. The agency did not disclose the specific livestock losses involved.

The action comes as Colorado's reintroduced wolf population continues to face scrutiny from both ranching communities and conservation advocates. Uncollared wolves present additional management challenges because they cannot be tracked remotely.

stories.headline: Drought Drives Spike in Bear Conflicts Across Colorado's Front Range; Bear Relocated from Louisville
stories.summary:
Colorado Parks and Wildlife relocated an adult male black bear from Louisville on Tuesday after the animal spent several days in the area and failed to move on its own. Officials darted and safely released the bear into more suitable habitat, with no injuries reported.

CPW says bear reports and conflicts have increased significantly this year, with drought identified as the primary driver. Depleted natural food sources push bears toward populated areas in search of calories, increasing the risk of dangerous encounters with humans and property.

The agency is urging residents across the Front Range to keep trash secured and inaccessible to bears. Officials stressed that feeding bears — even inadvertently through unsecured garbage — is harmful to the animals and escalates conflict with humans.

stories.headline: Native Roots Closes Denver Cannabis Grow Facility, Lays Off 141 Employees Following Dispensary Sale
stories.summary:
Colorado cannabis company Native Roots is closing its Denver grow facility and laying off 141 employees after Verdant Capital Partners acquired 15 of its retail dispensary locations. The transaction marks a significant restructuring for one of Colorado's larger cannabis operators.

The layoffs represent a substantial workforce reduction tied directly to the change in ownership of the retail side of the business. Details on the timeline for the facility closure and the terms of the acquisition were not fully disclosed.

The development reflects continued consolidation pressure in Colorado's cannabis industry, where operators have faced margin compression, increased competition, and a challenging regulatory environment in recent years.

stories.headline: Mi Pueblo Market to Open Largest Location at Former Westminster Walmart Site
stories.summary:
Mi Pueblo Market plans to transform a former Walmart location in Westminster into its sixth metro-area store, which would also be its largest. The grocer projects the new location will generate approximately $270 million in sales over its first five years of operation.

The move continues a broader trend of regional and specialty grocers repurposing large-format retail spaces left vacant by big-box store closures. The Westminster site's size is expected to allow Mi Pueblo to significantly expand its footprint and product offerings compared to its existing locations.

Mi Pueblo Market serves a predominantly Hispanic customer base and has been expanding its presence in the Denver metro area. The Westminster opening would extend its reach into Adams County's growing suburban market.

stories.headline: CenturyLink Phasing Out Colorado Landline Service, Shifting Remaining Customers to Wireless Option
stories.summary:
CenturyLink has begun notifying Colorado customers along the Front Range that it is discontinuing legacy landline voice service and transitioning them to a wireless alternative called Connected Voice with Air-Line. The company has requested FCC permission to end existing fiber voice service for customers from Fort Collins to Fountain, effective August 24.

The transition stems from AT&T's acquisition of CenturyLink's consumer fiber network last year. AT&T is unwilling to allow CenturyLink continued use of the fiber infrastructure, and CenturyLink has opted not to revert to its older copper network. Federal law requires customers receive a minimum of 90 days' notice to switch providers or adopt the new service.

The Air-Line wireless option uses a small adapter that routes calls through a nearby cellular tower while maintaining existing phone equipment, caller ID, and familiar dial tones. A battery backup accessory is available to preserve service during power outages.

CenturyLink spokesman Ron Boehmer confirmed the company plans to ultimately shut down its remaining copper network, though no specific timeline has been announced. The number of affected Colorado customers was not disclosed.

stories.headline: Denver HOA Foreclosure Case Heads to Colorado Supreme Court, Displaced Family Remains in Limbo
stories.summary:
A legal battle over the foreclosure sale of an affordable home in Denver's Green Valley Ranch neighborhood has reached the Colorado Supreme Court after an investor challenged two lower court rulings in favor of the city. The case centers on Monica Villela's home, which a Denver district judge ruled should never have been sold to Welcome to Realty LLC following an HOA-related foreclosure auction.

The Colorado Court of Appeals earlier this year sided with Denver, which argues its inclusionary housing ordinance — which places price caps on certain homes to keep them affordable — takes precedence over a homeowners association or metro district lien. The investor, Christophe Attard, contends the rulings could overturn a 48-year-old Colorado precedent that gives special districts super-priority liens over mortgages.

The Special District Association of Colorado has filed a brief supporting Welcome to Realty, arguing that special districts — which fund libraries, fire departments, and water services — depend on lien authority to ensure stable revenue for future planning. The association says the lower court decisions threaten the financial foundation of local governance across the state.

Meanwhile, Villela and her four children remain displaced, staying with family while the legal process continues. Supporters have raised enough money to purchase the home back from Attard, but he has reportedly declined the offer.

stories.headline: Denver Nuggets Sign Lonnie Walker IV to One-Year, $3.3 Million Deal
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets have agreed to a one-year, $3.3 million contract with wing Lonnie Walker IV, according to an ESPN report. Walker, 27, most recently played for Israeli club Maccabi Tel Aviv and had a short stint with the Philadelphia 76ers in 2024-25, averaging 12.4 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.5 assists in 20 games.

Walker was the 18th overall pick in the 2018 NBA Draft out of the University of Miami and has previously played for the San Antonio Spurs, Los Angeles Lakers, Brooklyn Nets, and 76ers, in addition to stints with European clubs in Lithuania and Israel. He is a career 42% shooter from the field and has shot 36% from three-point range.

With Walker's signing, Denver will have 14 of 15 standard roster spots filled once the deal becomes official. Restricted free agent Peyton Watson remains unsigned, with sign-and-trade discussions involving the Atlanta Hawks ongoing. Walker is the second EuroLeague player the Nuggets have signed this offseason, following Alpha Diallo from AS Monaco.

stories.headline: Colorado 14er Visitation Hit Decade Low in 2025, Driven by Mount Blue Sky Road Closure
stories.summary:
Visitation to Colorado's 14,000-foot peaks fell to its lowest level in a decade in 2025, with the Colorado Fourteeners Initiative recording 256,000 hiker-use days — down 3% from 2024. The decline was driven largely by the closure of the Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway for construction, which reduced visitation to that peak from as many as 25,000 hiker-use days in 2024 to just 1,000 to 3,000 last year.

Mount Bierstadt was the most visited 14er in 2025 with an estimated 31,000 hiker-use days, followed by Quandary Peak at 30,500, both higher than 2024 figures. CFI attributed the increases at other peaks partly to hikers displaced from Mount Blue Sky seeking alternatives. The byway reopened in May of this year.

Front Range peaks continued to dominate overall use, accounting for 59% of all hiker-use days. The San Juan Mountains saw a 30% drop in visitation and the Elk Mountains fell 17%, while the Sangre de Cristo Mountains recorded a 65% increase — though from a smaller baseline.

CFI executive director Lloyd F. Athearn said the data masks an underlying trend of continued strong demand for 14er recreation. The nonprofit has tracked hiker-use estimates annually since 2015.

topStory.headline: Iran Says Strait of Hormuz Deal With Oman in 'Final Stage' as U.S. Presses for Quick Agreement
topStory.summary:
Iran announced Wednesday that negotiations with Oman over reopening the Strait of Hormuz have reached their "final stage," with Iranian and Omani negotiators having finalized a draft agreement that now awaits approval from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. President Donald Trump said earlier this week that a deal could be announced within days, telling reporters the strait would be open "very soon." Iranian sources, however, pushed back on Trump's characterization of imminent agreement, saying important details remain unresolved.

The proposed arrangement would give Iran some measure of control over ships entering the Persian Gulf through the strait, with Oman overseeing outbound shipping traffic through the waterway. Iran has also conditioned reopening the strait on the United States lifting its blockade of Iranian ports — a demand that complicates the negotiations, as the Trump administration had previously ruled out any deal that would cement Iran's grip over the passage. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said talks with Oman have been "positive" but warned that "certain parties" could still obstruct a final agreement.

The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to normal commercial traffic since the United States and Israel launched military operations against Iran on February 28, citing goals that included ending Tehran's nuclear program and toppling its government. Before the conflict, roughly 130 ships transited the strait daily, carrying approximately one-fifth of the world's traded oil and natural gas; that figure has fallen to as few as eight vessels per day. The closure has driven up fuel and consumer goods prices worldwide and is widely described as a drag on the global economy.

Oman, whose territorial waters border the strait, has served as a long-standing back-channel mediator between Washington and Tehran. Iran has denied holding direct talks with the United States, maintaining that its discussions are with Oman exclusively. Khamenei, believed to have been wounded in the opening strikes of the war, has not appeared publicly since late February, and regional officials said the draft deal awaits his final authorization.

A deal on the strait is described by officials as a temporary measure intended to create space for broader negotiations, including resumed talks on Iran's nuclear program. The diplomatic effort also comes as related conflicts simmer: Houthi forces in Yemen reported missile strikes on two additional Saudi oil tankers, two Israeli soldiers were killed in southern Lebanon in what the Israeli military described as an explosion at a site near the village of Majdal Zoun, and U.S.-backed talks between Israel and Lebanon in Rome were cut short Wednesday amid disputes between the delegations. Trump faces mounting political pressure to end the war before U.S. congressional elections.
